clue.text: Cries of excitement from women's steel bands

parts.note: W is the standard abbreviation for women
hoops are metal bands, as round a barrel

explanation.surface: Female steel-band players draw shouts of excitement from the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steel bands' suggests Caribbean music, but here it means metal rings round a barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Shouts of delight or glee are exactly what such exclamations are.

clue.text: Rubbish reported on track that's ruined by corporation

indicators.note: signals that the word for rubbish is heard, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: waste is rubbish
a railway line is a track

explanation.surface: Gossip about a railway line spoiled by a big company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' is the old jocular word for a pot belly, which spoils one's figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A paunch, jokingly called a corporation, ruins the trimness of one's middle.

clue.text: Tyrannise work-force

parts.note: op. (opus) is a musical work
to press is to force

explanation.surface: A dictator rules over the labour force.
explanation.definitionFit: To rule cruelly and keep people down is to be tyrannical.

clue.text: Minister has to wed in country style

parts.note: a pastor is a church minister
to ally is to join or unite, as in marriage

explanation.surface: A clergyman must marry in a rustic setting.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastoral means rural, relating to the countryside.

clue.text: Craving an analgesic by midnight

parts.note: aspirin is a common painkiller

indicators.note: 'midnight' read as the middle of the word night, which is its central letter

explanation.surface: Someone longs for a painkiller late at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'midnight' splits as 'mid' + 'night': the middle letter of NIGHT is G.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean longing or eagerly desiring something.

clue.text: Girls' game in northern buffet dance

parts.note: in northern English dialect a buffet is a low stool
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Girls play a game at a dance with a northern buffet supper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buffet' looks like a spread of food, but in the north of England it is a footstool. STOOLBALL is an old English bat-and-ball game, traditionally played by girls.
explanation.definitionFit: An old English bat-and-ball sport historically played by milkmaids and women.

clue.text: Shooting this in US gun club

explanation.definitionFit: The metal names a firearm in American slang and a golf club.

clue.text: Send to Coventry one so tardy

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
late means tardy

explanation.surface: A latecomer is shunned for being so tardy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Send to Coventry' is a British idiom meaning to ostracise, refuse to speak to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostracising someone sets them apart from the group.

clue.text: Great enjoyment, tucking into asparagus tops

indicators.note: the letters are found within the run of words, as if eaten into them

explanation.surface: Someone eats asparagus tips with relish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' suggests eating, but signals the letters sit inside 'asparagus tops'.
explanation.definitionFit: Zest and relish are synonyms for hearty enjoyment.

clue.text: Cheese provided by 6, thanks

parts.note: refers to the answer at 6 down, a metal whose chemical symbol is Fe
ta is British slang for thanks

explanation.surface: Someone thanks another for supplying some cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: A white brined Greek cheese made from sheep's or goat's milk.

clue.text: Deadlock that's broken by politician meeting fool

indicators.note: the abbreviation for 'that is' is split open with the other pieces placed inside it

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of Latin id est, 'that is'
MP is a Member of Parliament
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A stalemate is ended when a politician meets an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken by' signals a container: the abbreviation for 'that is' is split open, not a deadlock being broken.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalemate where no progress is possible is a standard synonym.

clue.text: Outdoors without a sort of shirt, perhaps — it's balmy

indicators.note: signals the remaining letters may be rearranged into another form
the letter for a kind of shirt is taken out of the word outdoors

parts.note: a T-shirt is a sort of shirt, so T

explanation.surface: Going outside without a shirt on a pleasant, mild day.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove T (as in T-shirt) from OUTDOORS to leave OUDOORS; 'perhaps' tells you to rearrange those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Balmy in its older sense means fragrant, sweet-smelling like balm.

clue.text: Place where one has to drive absolutely soberly

parts.words: Place where one has to drive
parts.note: a golfer drives off from the tee
totally means absolutely, completely

explanation.surface: A warning that motorists must stay completely sober.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drive' suggests a car, but it is the golfer's long first shot from the tee.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstaining from all alcohol is acting soberly in the strictest way.

clue.text: Headlight a new driver's showing inside small building

indicators.note: the article and the learner's letter are placed within the abbreviation for house

parts.note: HO is the abbreviation for house
L is the learner plate shown by a new driver

explanation.surface: A learner driver's headlight is on inside a small garage.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a new driver displays an L plate, hence L.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring of light round a saint's head is literally a light on the head.

clue.text: After bolting, locking it is of little use

definitions.text: After bolting, locking it is of little use

parts.words: After bolting, locking it is of little use
parts.note: the proverb about shutting the barn entrance after the horse has bolted, too late to help

explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says it is pointless securing it once the horse has escaped.

clue.text: Sort of coffee for making a shake

definitions.meaning: a powdered coffee made quickly by adding hot water
'in two shakes' means in a moment, a very short time

explanation.definitionFit: Powdered coffee is named for its speed, and a shake is a moment.

clue.text: High social position of PRA?

definitions.meaning: the upper class, the highest rank
the President of the Royal Academy is the top artist, a top painter or draughtsman

explanation.walkthrough: PRA is President of the Royal Academy, Britain's leading art institution.
explanation.definitionFit: Upper-class people are top-ranking, and the PRA is the leading artist.

clue.text: She makes entrance to house, putting key in a lock

indicators.note: the musical key is placed within 'a lock'

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair
C is a musical key

explanation.surface: A woman lets herself into the house by putting her key in the lock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house' is the theatre audience, and 'entrance' is coming on stage, not opening a front door.
explanation.definitionFit: A female performer makes her entrance onto the stage before the theatre audience.

clue.text: Bowled over, lost one's footing

explanation.definitionFit: Being amazed and lurching unsteadily are both expressed by the same verb.

clue.text: Hide from gasbag endlessly

indicators.note: the last letter of the word for the gasbag is dropped

parts.note: the envelope is the gas-holding bag of a balloon or airship

explanation.surface: Someone takes cover from a long-winded talker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gasbag' looks like a chatterbox, but it is the bag holding a balloon's gas.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrap something completely is to cover and conceal it.

clue.text: Wild flower absorbing nitrogen

indicators.note: the flower takes in the element's symbol

parts.note: the violet is a flower
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: A wild plant takes up nitrogen from the soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild flower' reads as one phrase, but 'Wild' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferocious, uncontrolled behaviour is wild.

clue.text: Note about suspicious marks in plant

indicators.note: the note goes round the other piece

parts.note: la is a note of the sol-fa scale
obeli are marks used to flag doubtful or spurious passages in texts

explanation.surface: Odd markings are spotted on a garden plant.
explanation.walkthrough: An obelus (plural obeli) is a dagger-like mark editors use to flag doubtful text.
explanation.definitionFit: A low flowering garden bedding species, often blue.

clue.text: Beastly chap having one over the eight

parts.note: Leo is a man's name
nine is one more than eight; 'one over the eight' is also British slang for slightly drunk

explanation.surface: A nasty fellow who has had a drink too many.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one over the eight' is a British idiom for being a bit drunk, here read literally as nine.
explanation.definitionFit: Lion-like, resembling a wild animal, the king of beasts.

clue.text: Bird used in humble pie in US?

definitions.meaning: a black bird of the genus Corvus

definitions.text: used in humble pie in US?
definitions.meaning: Americans 'eat ...' where the British eat humble pie

explanation.definitionFit: The black corvid is both a common bird and the American idiom for humiliation.

clue.text: Mount getting caught on a branch

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a limb is a large branch of a tree

explanation.surface: A climber's mount gets snagged on a tree branch.
explanation.definitionFit: To mount is to ascend.

clue.text: Composing music for children

parts.note: not writing tunes: 'composing' means calming, so this is music that soothes little ones to sleep

explanation.definitionFit: A lullaby is a gentle piece sung to settle a baby.

clue.text: Pack dress

explanation.definitionFit: A set of playing cards, and to adorn with finery.

clue.text: Man previously in charge of meeting I ran

definitions.text: Man previously in charge of meeting I ran

parts.words: Man previously in charge of meeting I ran
parts.note: 'meeting I ran' read as the words I and RAN joined, a country once ruled by a monarch now gone

explanation.definitionFit: The former king of Iran was titled thus until the 1979 revolution.

clue.text: Choctaws and Mohawks appear in this entertainment

definitions.text: Choctaws and Mohawks appear in this entertainment

parts.words: Choctaws and Mohawks appear in this entertainment
parts.note: not Native American peoples but two turns in figure skating, seen in a performance on the rink

explanation.definitionFit: A skating spectacle features figure-skating turns such as the choctaw and mohawk.

clue.text: Bishop's staff making many more hopeful

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100, hence many
rosier means more optimistic

explanation.surface: A bishop's assistants are becoming far more optimistic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' suggests employees, but it is the crook a bishop carries.
explanation.definitionFit: The hooked crook carried by a bishop as a symbol of office.

clue.text: A look like this kills

definitions.meaning: a ... hook is rhyming slang for a look
slaughters, as a meat trader does animals

explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang 'have a butcher's' (butcher's hook = look) means have a look.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyming slang gives the glance, and the verb for slaughtering gives the killing.

clue.text: Familiar member of society

definitions.meaning: a member of the Society of ..., a Quaker

explanation.definitionFit: A familiar is an intimate companion, and Quakers belong to the Religious Society of Friends.
